scope: Retrospective comparison on ten unique actual model memos. Same-assistant guard annotations measure errors. Fallback uses the existing case-specific reference renderer on matching evidence. Format and critical guard remain distinct.

original/39cbdf8f18.memo: Workshop status: IMPASSE. The first delegate holds the "review" card, while the second delegate holds the "closure" card. Since delegates accepted different packages, the chair recommends no package, matching the impasse status. The official record shows France and the UAE proposed S/2023/638 (13 for, 1 against, 1 abstention), which failed due to Russia's veto. Russia's separate draft S/2023/639 (1 for, 1 against, 13 abstentions) also failed. Workshop actions are merely recommendations with no official authority to change official votes.

original/951cd31a6d.memo: Workshop status: IMPASSE. The first delegate holds the "review" card, while the second delegate holds the "closure" card. Since neither delegate accepted the same package, the chair recommends no action. This aligns with the official record where draft S/2023/638 failed due to a Russian veto (13 for, 1 against, 1 abstention) and S/2023/639 failed due to insufficient support (1 for, 1 against, 13 abstentions). The workshop lacks official authority; its actions are merely recommendations. No missing card was identified in the current evidence.

original/65b2d68869.memo: Workshop status: UNRESOLVED. The chair holds a "review" card from the first delegate. No second delegate card is available, creating an impasse per public rules. The workshop recommends reviewing draft S/2023/638 (France/ UAE) and S/2023/639 (Russia) regarding Mali sanctions; both failed adoption due to negative votes from permanent members (Russia for 638, Japan for 639). The workshop lacks official authority to change official votes or adopt resolutions. Its only function is to recommend packages based on delegate acceptance. No official disposition is recorded.

original/2ac8218a1e.memo: Workshop status: EARLY. The UN office holds the "early only" card, while the liaison office holds the "both" card, forwarded by the UN office. These cards support the early status as the only overlapping slot. The official record mandates an oral report on UN support for the Five-Point Consensus by 15 March 2023, requiring immediate action on violence and humanitarian access. No missing cards are unavailable; both offices possess valid slots. Workshop actions remain recommendations with no official authority, serving solely to coordinate scheduling for the mandated briefing.

original/ec888e71dc.memo: Workshop status: EARLY. The UN office holds the "early only" card, while the liaison office holds the "both" card. This overlap supports the early slot selection. The official record mandates an oral report on UN support for the Five-Point Consensus by 15 March 2023, requiring immediate action on violence and humanitarian access. No missing cards are present. original/4fd43f211b.memo: Workshop status: UNRESOLVED. The UN office holds the "early only" card, while the liaison office holds the "late only" card. These non-overlapping slots prevent a joint briefing, necessitating a rescheduling request per the public rule. The reporting mandate for Resolution 2669 remains active regardless of this scheduling failure. The workshop lacks official authority; all actions are merely recommendations. For Mali, the draft symbols indicate a failure to coordinate due to the missing "both slots" card. For Myanmar, the authority lies solely in the Secretary-General's duty to report by 15 March 2023. The missing card required to resolve the deadlock is the "both slots" availability from either office.

retest/a1fe5c7842.memo: Workshop status: UNRESOLVED. The chair holds a "review" card from the first delegate. The second delegate's card is missing. This absence prevents a recommendation, as the public rule requires both delegates to accept the same package. The linked official record shows Status-638 failed due to a Russian veto (13-1-1), while Status-639 failed with only one vote in favor (1-1-13). Both drafts regarding Mali sanctions and the Panel of Experts were rejected by permanent members. The workshop can only offer recommendations; it lacks official authority to change votes or adopt resolutions.

retest/f31d0d5be7.memo: Workshop status: UNRESOLVED. The chair holds a "review" card from the first delegate, supporting the recommendation to review draft S/2023/638 (France/UAE) and S/2023/639 (Russia). Both drafts failed adoption: S/2023/638 due to Russia's sole negative vote (13-1-1), and S/2023/639 due to Japan's negative vote (1-1-13). The second delegate's card is missing; its absence prevents a recommendation. The workshop authority is limited to recommendations only, with no power to alter official votes or resolve the impasse caused by the missing evidence.

retest/685882e3e0.memo: Workshop status: UNRESOLVED. The UN office holds the "early only" card, while the liaison office holds the "late only" card. These non-overlapping slots prevent a joint briefing, necessitating a rescheduling request per the public rule. The official record mandates an oral report on UN support for the Five-Point Consensus under Resolution 2669, with a deadline of 15 March 2023. The reporting duty falls to the Secretary-General or Special Envoy, coordinating with the ASEAN Special Envoy. The missing card is the liaison office's "early only" option. Workshop actions remain recommendations with no official authority; the reporting mandate persists regardless of scheduling outcomes.

retest/ee81f3c1fe.memo: Workshop status: UNRESOLVED. The UN office holds the "early only" card, while the liaison office's card is missing. This gap prevents finding a briefing slot where both offices can attend, as the UN requires early timing and the liaison requires late timing. The historical record confirms Resolution 2669 mandates an oral report on UN support for the Five-Point Consensus by 15 March 2023. The workshop recommends rescheduling to find a compatible time but lacks authority to alter the reporting mandate or deadline. The decision remains pending the arrival of the liaison office's card.
